intro: You're looking for the best IR35 adviser near you, so you want someone local who can properly assess your employment status and help you respond to a status determination. Whether you're a contractor facing an inside determination or a client trying to get it right, the right adviser will look at your contract and working practices together. Here's how to judge who's best for your situation and what to have ready when you enquire.
need_heading: What people searching for the best IR35 adviser near me usually need
need_lead: Most people searching this phrase want clear, local guidance on whether their working arrangements fall inside or outside IR35, and what to do next.
needs: You're a contractor who has received an inside IR35 determination from a medium or large client and you want to understand whether it's correct and how to respond.
You're a client engaging contractors and you need to decide status properly, knowing that as a medium or large client the decision rests with you.
You want your contract looked at alongside your actual working practices, because the two must match and working practices often carry more weight.
You're facing a disagreement with a client over a status determination and want advice on how to raise a dispute or challenge the decision.
You're setting up as a contractor or taking on your first engagement and want to get the IR35 position right from the start rather than fix it later.
context_heading: Why 'best' and 'near me' matter for IR35 advice
context: There's no official ranking of IR35 advisers, so 'best' is really about finding someone whose experience matches your situation and who can explain their reasoning clearly. Look for a tax adviser or accountant with specific IR35 knowledge, and ask how they keep up with changes to off-payroll working rules.

'Near me' can be useful if you prefer face-to-face meetings, but many advisers work remotely across the UK. What matters most is that they understand your contract and working practices in detail, and that you feel comfortable asking them to explain the status decision step by step.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Say whether you're a contractor or a client, and whether the end client is in the private or public sector.
Describe the work you do and how you do it, including who controls what you do and when.
Mention whether you've already received a status determination and, if so, what it said.
Explain whether your contract has been looked at before and whether it matches how you actually work.
Say if there's a disagreement with the client over status, and what stage it's reached.
Give your location and whether you'd prefer to meet in person or are happy with remote advice.
questions: What experience do you have with IR35 cases like mine?
Will you look at both my contract and my actual working practices?
How do you keep up to date with changes to off-payroll working rules?
If I disagree with a client's status determination, how would you help me raise a dispute?
What qualifications and professional body memberships do you hold?
Are you supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes and do you have professional indemnity insurance?

faqs.q: What does an IR35 adviser actually do?
faqs.a: An IR35 adviser looks at your contract and working practices to assess employment status, and helps contractors and clients respond to status determinations. They can also help you prepare for or challenge a determination.

faqs.q: Do I need a local adviser for IR35?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. Many advisers work remotely, but if you prefer face-to-face meetings, searching 'near me' can help you find someone local. What matters most is their specific IR35 experience.

faqs.q: Who makes the IR35 status decision?
faqs.a: For medium and large clients, the client makes the status decision. As a contractor, you can dispute a determination if you believe it's wrong, and an adviser can help you with that.

faqs.q: How can I judge if an adviser is the best for me?
faqs.a: There's no official ranking, so ask about their experience with IR35, their qualifications, and whether they'll look at both your contract and working practices. A good adviser will explain their reasoning clearly and answer your questions.

extra_heading: Common misunderstandings about finding the best IR35 adviser near you
extra: A frequent misunderstanding is that a local adviser will automatically know your client's sector or your industry better than someone further away. What actually matters is whether they have handled IR35 questions like yours before, so ask them to talk you through how they would approach your contract and working practices rather than assuming proximity equals insight.

Another common assumption is that the adviser decides your status. For medium and large clients, the client makes the status decision, and your adviser's role is to assess the position, explain the reasoning and help you respond or raise a dispute if you disagree. Knowing this upfront stops you expecting an adviser to overrule a determination on your behalf.

People also often think a single read of the contract settles the question. Working practices matter as much as the contract, so a good adviser will want to talk about how you actually do the work, who directs it and how your engagement runs day to day before giving a view.

extra_faqs.q: Will a local IR35 adviser know my client's business?
extra_faqs.a: Not necessarily, and that is not the main thing to check. Ask instead about their experience of IR35 questions in situations like yours and how they would review both your contract and your working practices.

extra_faqs.q: Can an adviser change my client's status determination?
extra_faqs.a: No. For medium and large clients the client makes the decision. An adviser can assess whether it looks right, explain why, and help you raise a dispute with the client if you believe it is wrong.

extra_faqs.q: Is the contract on its own enough for an IR35 review?
extra_faqs.a: Usually not. Working practices matter as much as the contract, so expect questions about how you actually carry out the work, who controls it and how the engagement operates in practice.
